clue.text: Photographer briefly a neighbour to Oscar

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so only the opening of the long word is kept

explanation.surface: A paparazzo lives next door to someone called Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: PAP is the short form of paparazzo; add A to get PAPA.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet the codeword for P comes straight after the codeword for O, so they sit side by side.

clue.text: Benefit ultimately debatable with money wasted  - drivers' warning

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word it follows
something wasted is thrown away, so that element is dropped from the word

blocks.note: a moot point is one open to debate
M is the standard abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: An argument about whether a benefit is worth having, with cash squandered, followed by a warning to motorists.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the standard crossword abbreviation for money; a moot point is one still open to argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A toot is a short blast of a car horn, the usual way motorists alert others to danger.

clue.text: Charge politician and sweetheart to enter Toulouse's ground

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so these letters are placed within the other word

blocks.note: French for stadium, as a team from Toulouse would call its ground
the heart, or middle letter, of sweet

explanation.surface: An MP and a partner are charged with breaking into a French rugby stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweetheart looks like a lover, but it means the centre of the word sweet. Toulouse signals that the ground is named in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden mass rush forward, as when a herd of cattle charges in panic.

clue.text: London band finish up in service

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards
in places the first word inside the following one

blocks.note: the start of MASS, a church service

explanation.surface: A London group play out their last number at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'London band' could suggest a strip of the city, but it is the pop group; service is the Catholic Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: Madness are a ska and pop group formed in Camden, north London, in the late 1970s, famous for 'Our House'.

clue.text: Receiver regularly takes money to Arabs

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of takes
the rial is the currency of several Arab states such as Oman and Yemen

explanation.surface: Someone receiving stolen goods routinely takes cash to Arab traders.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerial is an antenna, the device on a radio or television that picks up broadcast signals.

clue.text: Stop working on highway

blocks.note: re means on the subject of, concerning
ST is the abbreviation for street, a public road

explanation.surface: Taking a break while out on the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To rest is to pause from labour and relax for a while, ceasing activity.

clue.text: Pointless opening bitter

indicators.note: pointless means without a point, a compass point being one of N, S, E or W, so one such letter is removed

explanation.surface: A pointless start that leaves a bitter taste.
explanation.walkthrough: START loses S, the south compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Tart describes a sharp, sour taste, close in sense to acidic or sharp flavours like lemon.

clue.text: U-turn in Indianapolis on F1

blocks.note: about means on the subject of
an ace counts as one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: A racing car turns round at the Indianapolis circuit during a Formula One race.
explanation.walkthrough: F1 looks like Formula One, but it is just F followed by 1. 'In Indianapolis' flags the American phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: About-face is the American term for a complete reversal of direction or opinion, the British equivalent being about-turn.

clue.text: One's sat by guitar when back with Motörhead

indicators.note: going back means the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: axe is slang for a guitar
the head, or first letter, of the band's name

explanation.surface: Someone sits beside a heavy metal guitar after returning to the band Motörhead.
explanation.walkthrough: AXE turned back is EXA, then M from the head of Motörhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Students sit an exam, so a test taken in a hall is something that is sat.

clue.text: Strange Martian? He's not one

indicators.note: something strange is out of the ordinary, so the letters are put in an unusual order
not one says the letter standing for one is left out

explanation.surface: An odd alien who insists he is not really one.
explanation.walkthrough: Add HE to MARTIAN, drop the I, and rearrange. Read whole, the clue is also the definition: a weird Martian who is not a Martian at all.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthman is a human from our own planet, which is exactly what a creature from Mars is not.

clue.text: Home town's extremely welcoming - absolutely

indicators.note: welcoming means letting someone in, so one element takes another inside

blocks.note: T is an abbreviation for town, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A hometown that is extremely hospitable through and through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home town' wants to be read as one phrase; split them. T for town is a map and sports abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: In toto is Latin for 'in total', meaning completely or entirely, the same sense as absolutely.

clue.text: Ignoring banks, might have borrowed

indicators.note: the banks of a river are its two edges, so ignoring them removes both outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone who stays away from banks may have taken out a loan elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: POWER loses its first and last letters. 'Banks' suggests money lenders, but here it means edges.
explanation.definitionFit: To owe money is to be in debt, which is the position of anyone who has taken a loan.

clue.text: Getting on to college head for being unfriendly

blocks.note: C is an abbreviation for college
someone getting on in years is old
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: An ageing college head gets a reputation for aloofness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'College head' reads as a principal, but head is a headland here, as in place names like Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Coldness is a lack of warmth in manner, the state of a person who is aloof and distant.

clue.text: 'Beware!' Post section's review for Carmen?

indicators.note: a section is a slice taken from within a longer stretch of text
to review is to look back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A newspaper warns readers before its review of a production of Carmen.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across bewARE Post, read backwards. The question mark marks Carmen as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmen is Bizet's famous French work for the stage, sung throughout, so it is one example of the genre.

clue.text: Hated change, bit upsetting - it's very dangerous

definitions.note: a clause standing for a noun: something that is very dangerous

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so the letters are rearranged
in a down entry, upsetting turns the word upside down so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: Someone loathed a change and found it rather upsetting, warning that it is risky.
explanation.definitionFit: A death trap is a building, vehicle or place so hazardous that it could easily kill someone.

clue.text: Complaint by City people against United's number 4

indicators.note: number 4 picks out the fourth letter of the word

blocks.note: U-N-I-T: the fourth letter of United

explanation.surface: Manchester City fans grumble about United's number four player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' and 'United' suggest the Manchester football rivals, but City is just LA. 'Against' simply places the last piece next to the others.
explanation.definitionFit: A lament is an expression of grief or regret, so a complaint or wail of sorrow.

clue.text: Little time to get tea or coffee

blocks.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Someone with only a moment to spare deciding between tea and coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea or coffee' looks like a choice of drinks for the definition, but only coffee defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine-quality coffee, originally shipped from the Yemeni port of that name, often flavoured with chocolate.

clue.text: Reminder government's totally exposed

blocks.note: G is an abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: A reminder that the government's dealings have been laid completely bare.
explanation.walkthrough: G sits inside NUDE; the 's acts as 'is' joining the pieces, so G is contained.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a gentle prompt or poke to remind someone to do something.

clue.text: Reversed with an edge restored? About time

indicators.note: something restored has been reworked, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the other

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A blade that has been turned round so its edge is sharpened again, just in time.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate a decision is to cancel or undo it, just as a reversed ruling is overturned.

clue.text: Virginia rejected online supermarket fruit

indicators.note: to reject is to send back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: Ocado is a British internet grocer that delivers to homes

explanation.surface: A shopper called Virginia sends back fruit ordered from a grocery delivery website.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is the pear-shaped green fruit of a tropical tree, eaten in salads and guacamole.

clue.text: Writer's picked up van - it's broken down outside A&E?

indicators.note: in a down entry, picked up lifts the letters so they read from bottom to top
something broken down has fallen to pieces, so the letters are reassembled
outside puts the jumbled letters around the other piece

blocks.note: writer is the setter, so writer's is I am, shortened

explanation.surface: The setter's van has broken down and been taken to hospital casualty.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is a British hospital's accident and emergency department, but here it is two letters. MI sits inside the jumbled VITANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitamin A and vitamin E are two essential nutrients; the question mark flags this definition by example.

clue.text: That's a joke about road 'improvement' - ultimately it's a safety issue

definitions.text: That's a joke about road 'improvement' - ultimately it's a safety issue

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the laugh goes round the other piece
ultimately picks out the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: the sound of laughter at a joke

explanation.surface: A sarcastic remark about roadworks, ending with a point about safety.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also describes the gear road workers are issued during so-called improvements; the quotation marks mock the roadworks.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard hat is the protective helmet issued to workers on building sites and roadworks.

clue.text: Wooden actor in county town

blocks.note: a ham is an overacting performer

explanation.surface: A stiff, unconvincing performer appears in a provincial town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wooden actor' reads as a poor performer, but it splits into two pieces. Rutland is England's smallest county.
explanation.definitionFit: Oakham is the administrative centre of Rutland, making it that county's principal town.

clue.text: Drink Church of Scotland finally banned

indicators.note: the final letter is banned, so the word loses its end

blocks.note: the Kirk is the Church of Scotland

explanation.surface: The Church of Scotland has at last prohibited alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Kir is a French aperitif made of white wine with a dash of blackcurrant liqueur, crème de cassis.

clue.text: City in African country's less than half-built

indicators.note: less than half means most of the word is cut away, keeping only a small opening portion

explanation.surface: A city in an African nation whose construction is not yet half done.
explanation.walkthrough: Of the five letters of built, two is less than half, giving BU.
explanation.definitionFit: Malibu is a beach city in Los Angeles County, California, known for celebrity homes and surfing.

clue.text: He'll get stuck into workers before subsequently dismissing leader

indicators.note: dismissing the leader sends away the first letter

blocks.note: ante is Latin for before, as in antenatal

explanation.surface: A boss who will tackle the workforce head-on, after first sacking the foreman.
explanation.walkthrough: Workers are ants in crosswords, and 'get stuck into' means tuck in to eat. LATER drops its L.
explanation.definitionFit: An anteater feeds on ants, the classic crossword workers, so it literally tucks into them.

clue.text: Price-fixers getting hump - felt unprotected

indicators.note: unprotected means without its outer cover, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: to hump is to carry, or cart, something heavy

explanation.surface: Members of a price-fixing ring get annoyed and feel exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting the hump' is British slang for getting annoyed, but hump is a verb meaning carry. FELT loses its edges.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartel is a group of companies that agree to control prices and limit competition.

clue.text: Sloth circling around berry

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the animal's letters surround the other piece

blocks.note: the ai is a three-toed sloth
ca is short for circa, meaning around

explanation.surface: A sloth in the rainforest wraps itself round a berry.
explanation.definitionFit: Acai is the small purple fruit of a Brazilian palm, marketed as a health food.

clue.text: See 15
Slander retracted by bishop who's sorry - no words are necessary here

indicators.note: retracted means drawn back, so the letters are read backwards
sorry means in a poor state, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: to sling mud is to slander
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop withdraws a slur and apologises; actions speak louder than words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorry' looks like the bishop apologising, but it jumbles the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumb show is a performance in mime, with gestures replacing speech entirely.

clue.text: Don't go by road, I agree

explanation.surface: Someone is urged not to drive off, and agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' just places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Stay is the imperative telling someone to remain where they are rather than leave.

clue.text: Mounting trouble besetting Spain's old theatres

indicators.note: in a down entry, mounting means climbing upward, so the letters read backwards
besetting means surrounding on all sides, so the other piece is enclosed

blocks.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Growing unrest surrounds Spain's ancient amphitheatres.
explanation.definitionFit: Odea (singular odeum) were roofed buildings in ancient Greece and Rome for musical performances.

clue.text: Recalled a little information

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read in the other direction

explanation.surface: Someone remembered a small amount of what they had been told.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures collected for reference or analysis, the raw material of knowledge.

clue.text: Trouble and a brief time when you can't think clearly

definitions.text: time when you can't think clearly

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so the following letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Problems and a short spell of mental fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief time' wants to go together, but brief belongs to the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain fade is a momentary lapse of concentration or memory, a mental blank.
